title: Bigger models and longer context on fixed GPU memory
subtitle: When GPU memory, not the workload, is the limit

stats.label: exact cells bit-identical to fully resident attention at the native port, 12 of 12 hybrid

sustained output throughput of the 4-bit build over the mixed 4- and 8-bit control, 64 clients

lede: A model's context, or the number of long sessions that can stay alive, is capped by the memory on the cards at hand. The usual answers are bigger cards, more cards or less context. I built an inference-memory layer for vLLM that moves a context's history into host RAM and treats the GPU as a bounded working set, with an exact tier that is bit-identical to fully resident attention. I ported it entirely to native C++ under parity gates, as a patch that applies to an unmodified vLLM. Start with Context beyond VRAM. I fit a 27-billion-parameter model on a single 32 GB Intel card through a published, measured quantization.
quote: Exactness is a property I want in the system.
evidence: KV-cache offload for LLM inference: a context's history in host RAM and the GPU as a bounded working set inside vLLM, with an exact tier bit-identical to fully resident attention in 13 of 13 cells.
C++ and native ports with parity proof: the memory layer ported entirely to native C++ under parity gates, 12 of 12 hybrid cells matching and 0 Python files in the release payload.
LLM quantization (4-bit): a 27B model fitted on one 32 GB Intel card as a W4A16 build, +36% sustained output throughput over the mixed control at a stated 3.33% perplexity cost.
Intel GPU and SYCL/oneAPI engineering: vendor kernel patches on new silicon with identical outputs, cutting a cold 32K-token prefill from 21.54 s to 17.23 s.
Performance benchmarking methodology: time to first token of 3.68 s against stock vLLM's 4.71 s on a single 8K request, with the 128K regime where stock still decodes faster stated beside it.
author: Corey James
